title: Override access safety-net procedures for emergency admin elevation and audit-forwarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a safe, auditable, and short-lived override (emergency elevation) path that allows on-call engineers or SREs to obtain time-limited admin privileges when normal access routes are unavailable (SSO outage, key misrotation, or critical incident). The flow must integrate with RBAC v2, enrich audit logs for forensic review, and require post-event attestation.

Scope:
- JIT override issuance with explicit approver or automated policy when approver unavailable.
- Ephemeral credentials (token + scoped session) with enforced TTL and automated revocation.
- Mandatory audit-stream enrichment: reason, incident ID, approver, requesting host, session traceback.
- Integration points: SSO/SAML assertion exchange, KMS-wrapped token storage, observability hooks (Console traces + SLO dashboard).

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term privileged user accounts.
- Designing a full-blown RBAC policy language (this is a safety-net feature).

Success criteria (MUST):
- Override issuance requires either (a) a 2nd-party human approver OR (b) multi-signal automated policy (pager duty + severity threshold + incident id) when approver path is down.
- Issued session TTL default 15 minutes, configurable up to 4 hours with strong justification and audit.
- Every override event appears in the immutable audit stream within 30s with fields: requester, approver_id (or policy_id), reason, TTL, session_token_hash, affected_resources, incident_id, and correlation_id.
- Automatic revocation on TTL expiry and on manual revoke; revocation logged and surfaced in Console.
- Post-incident attestation checklist completed within 72 hours or ticket escalated to Security.

Design summary:
1) Request: CLI/Console endpoint posts override request (includes incident_id, justification, requested_scope, requested_duration). Request is signed by the requester via SSO assertion when available.
2) Approval: Primary path is human approver (oncall rotation). Secondary path is automated policy evaluation (PagerDuty active oncall + incident severity >= critical + ops-channel acknowledgement). Logging middleware records why automated path was used.
3) Issuance: A short-lived session credential is minted by the Auth service; token is bound to session metadata and persisted as a KMS-wrapped audit artifact. Token is hashed in the audit stream (no raw tokens in logs).
4) Enforcement: RBAC v2 evaluates the scoped session and enforces least privilege. Any attempt to escalate beyond scope triggers an immediate revoke and alert.
5) Post-access: Requester must complete an attestation form (linked in the issuance response) and attach any incident artifacts. Lack of attestation opens an internal review.

Trade-offs considered:
- TTL length vs operational friction: 15m default balances safety & productivity; longer durations require explicit justification and Security approval.
- Human approval latency vs automated policy availability: we allow automated fallback for SSO outages but require multi-signal checks to reduce misuse risk.
- Audit granularity vs PII leakage: we log hashes of sensitive tokens and include metadata sufficient for forensics without storing credentials in plaintext.

Operational hooks and observability:
- Console: new "Override Events" stream with filters by user, resource, incident_id, approver, and time range.
- Alerts: security-oncall slack + email + PagerDuty trigger on any manual override, and on automated fallback issuance.
- Metrics: count of overrides/day, mean time to approval, TTL distribution, post-access attestation completion rate.

Rollback/fallback plan:
- If rollout causes false positives (legit workflows blocked), allow temporary broadening of a canary group via feature flag, with immediate audit and Security approval.
- If audit stream lag > 60s, automatically disable automated fallback path until stream health restored.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Override+Access+Safety+Net (working draft)
- Preliminary GitHub RFC/PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/472
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/override-console-mockups
comments: 2025-02-18 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after oncall reported inability to access admin routes during SSO outage. Initial design drafted and shared with Security. Next: finalize automated policy requirements.

2025-02-21 — Mariana Costa (Security): Reviewed design; requested stronger attestation and a required post-mortem for any override used outside test windows. Also asked for KMS wrapping for persisted session artifacts.

2025-02-25 — Liam Chen (Assignee): Implemented issuance prototype in auth-service, added token-hash in audit stream. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/891 — needs review from infra and security teams.

2025-02-27 — QA (J. Ramirez): Performed toy incident simulation; found that automated fallback triggered without PagerDuty binding in our staging environment. Root cause: service account used for PagerDuty API was expired. Action: add validity checks to automated-policy engine and better state reporting in Console.

2025-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Incorporated feedback — increased default TTL to 15m (was 10m), added explicit attestation link to issuance response, and added metrics tracked by Console. Marking In Review and requesting Security sign-off.
2025-03-01 — Liam Chen: Drafted runbook for oncall: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Runbooks/Override+Runbook. Please add any missing post-incident steps or audit queries that SRE needs.
